name: Yo La Tengo
label: Matador
lede: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley went through roughly fifteen bass players before James McNew stayed. Three decades on, the band still makes records that whisper, roar, and play eight nights of Hanukkah.

eras.title: A yellow tango in Hoboken
eras.text: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley, a couple in Hoboken, New Jersey, built a band out of shared records: The Soft Boys, Mission of Burma, Love. The line-ups changed almost every season; the two of them never did.

years.h: Ira Kaplan, a rock critic, and Georgia Hubley start a band in Hoboken
years.p: Hubley, a drummer, is the daughter of Oscar-winning animators John and Faith Hubley. The two build the band around their record collection, with [[Dave Rick|6a5eae3e-3ee8-44bc-90d4-33bcc59f5c74]] on bass.

years.big: What the hell is a yellow tango?
years.h: A 1962 Mets collision gives the band its name
years.p: Left fielder Frank Thomas's reported question after he ran into center fielder Richie Ashburn, who had been shouting the Spanish for "I've got it" at shortstop Elio Chacón.
years.xp:
Ashburn and Chacón kept colliding on fly balls, so Ashburn learned to yell yo la tengo. The next game, Thomas, who spoke no Spanish, crashed into Ashburn anyway.

Wikipedia flags the provenance as dubious: Thomas always insisted Ashburn made the whole thing up.

years.h: The first single, on Coyote, covers Arthur Lee
years.p: Late 1985's 7-inch pairs The River of Water with a cover of [[Arthur Lee|4e0a7e0d-bd05-4210-a654-72c4d437fda5]]'s A House Is Not a Motel. [[Dave Schramm|b06d3876-1fc4-4017-8cf9-da964b8a733a]] plays lead guitar.

years.h: Clint Conley of Mission of Burma produces Ride the Tiger
years.p: [[Clint Conley|a09560c0-4264-4341-af25-5727ca13417b]] also plays bass on three songs of the Coyote Records debut. The sleeve credits Kaplan with naive guitar.

years.h: Schramm and Mike Lewis quit; Kaplan takes lead guitar
years.p: After Ride the Tiger, guitarist Dave Schramm and bassist Mike Lewis both leave. [[Stephan Wichnewski|9ea87f74-92cb-4ba2-9e26-f01d39a29212]] joins on bass.

eras.title: The bass player carousel
eras.text: With Kaplan now on guitar, Yo La Tengo made its name with critics while cycling through bass players, and even played as a duo for a stretch. Fakebook showed the quiet side that would matter as much as the noise.

years.h: New Wave Hot Dogs leans into noise, and sells poorly
years.p: The second Coyote album moves past jangle toward more guitar noise.

years.h: Robert Christgau likes the opening hook on President Yo La Tengo
years.p: Robert Christgau praised the guitar hook of opener Barnaby, Hardly Working. [[Gene Holder|f35abb6b-cd8a-4f61-98c3-880e0d4a98dd]] of [[The dB's|d2a54937-fd0d-4586-85c3-235a405019cf]] produces the last Coyote album, and it makes the band's reputation.

years.h: Down to two: Kaplan and Hubley on two electric guitars
years.p: Stephan Wichnewski leaves. For a while Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley play shows as a two-piece.

years.h: Fakebook goes acoustic and covers Cat Stevens, the Kinks and Daniel Johnston
years.p: Schramm returns for a mostly acoustic Bar/None album of covers by [[Cat Stevens|e2345fdf-2be7-47c5-a6dd-be64353ad134]], [[Gene Clark|2b6f3780-6fb6-42c2-95bb-5e080772e38c]], [[The Kinks|17b53d9f-5c63-4a09-a593-dde4608e0db9]] and [[Daniel Johnston|8a7ca8b0-d23c-4eff-8fe9-6220ba5c9c76]], plus a quiet redo of Barnaby, Hardly Working.

years.h: Daniel Johnston records Speeding Motorcycle with the band behind him
years.p: The same year brings the That Is Yo La Tengo EP and a Beat Happening cover, Cast a Shadow.

years.h: James McNew signs on for one tour and stays
years.p: McNew, on leaving a box of merchandise at a club in Münster. He joined as a fill-in for a short US tour and a four-week European run with [[Eleventh Dream Day|751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a]], and is the last of roughly fifteen bassists.
years.xp:
McNew realized the mistake at soundcheck in Hamburg the next day, while Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley were away. Wikipedia prints his version: "Sure... blame it on the rookie."

By 1992 the three were a fixed trio, the line-up that has lasted since. McNew also records on his own as [[Dump|2d9215eb-0d46-4624-b155-2a0f32482a4e]].

eras.title: Three people, one sound
eras.text: James McNew was in, Roger Moutenot was producing, and the band signed to Matador Records. It found the balance of feedback and hush it still works from. By 1997 Pitchfork was handing out a 9.7.

years.h: Gene Holder produces May I Sing with Me in Boston
years.p: Lou Giordano engineers the Alias album. Three songs carry over from the That Is Yo La Tengo EP, with Holder on bass.

years.h: The Matador years start with a single, Shaker
years.p: Matador Records signs the band; Shaker is recorded with John Siket in New Jersey. The partnership has lasted more than thirty years.

years.big: I think this group really started when we made the record Painful
years.h: Painful starts a 20-year run with producer Roger Moutenot
years.p: Ira Kaplan's verdict on the first album with James McNew on every song. Rob Sheffield wrote that it kept every promise the band ever made.
years.xp:
Painful opens and closes with two versions of Big Day Coming, one a slow drone, one a buzzing rocker. From a Motel 6 became an early Matador favorite.

Stephen Thomas Erlewine called it "a subtly addicting album." Moutenot produced Yo La Tengo records until Fade in 2013.

yt: "When You Were Mine," live at Tramps, New York, 1995
years.h: Electr-O-Pura puts one credit on every song: Yo La Tengo
years.p: For the first time every song is credited to the band as a whole rather than to individuals. It stays that way.

years.h: They play an unnamed Velvet Underground in I Shot Andy Warhol
years.p: Critics had compared them to [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]] for years. In Mary Harron's film, the band appears as an anonymous version of it.

years.h: Pitchfork gives I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One a 9.7
years.p: Folk, punk, shoegaze drones, bossa nova and noise jams on one Matador album. AllMusic called it arguably the band's finest and most coherent.
years.xp:
Kaplan said that after Electr-O-Pura the band was "trying not to worry too hard about what the next album is going to sound like."

The result runs from the drone of Spec Bebop to the Beach Boys-style Sugarcube to Stockholm Syndrome, sung by James McNew.
play: I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One

years.h: Bob Odenkirk and David Cross run a rock school in the Sugarcube video
years.p: Both are of Mr. Show; Bob Odenkirk and David Cross star in the video for the song from I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One.

eras.title: Eight nights a year in Hoboken
eras.text: The next decade ran in every direction: whisper-quiet albums, film scores, a collaboration with Yoko Ono, radio marathons, and a Hanukkah residency that became a Hoboken tradition.

years.h: A Salvation Army band in Hal Hartley's The Book of Life
years.p: Yo La Tengo plays the part in Hal Hartley's film, and makes Strange but True with [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] of [[Half Japanese|18dc6bd7-9caa-4c2d-a2fc-e9546ebda6a4]].

years.h: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out closes on 17 minutes of Hoboken
years.p: The hushed album closes with Night Falls on Hoboken, named for the band's home town.
play: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out

years.h: Painlevé's undersea films get a Yo La Tengo score
years.p: The band scores eight documentaries by French filmmaker Jean Painlevé for the San Francisco Film Festival, as The Sounds of the Sounds of Science, then plays it live about a dozen times.

years.h: Maxwell's hosts all eight nights of Hanukkah
years.p: Yo La Tengo starts a run at Maxwell's in Hoboken with surprise guests and comedians and proceeds going to charity. It becomes an annual pilgrimage.

years.h: Kaplan drops the loud songs from Summer Sun at the last second
years.p: Some critics found the quiet album underwhelming. The same year, the band records with [[Yoko Ono|b0b33754-a664-43b7-ba00-be0dc4ec2396]] for a Harvey Milk High School benefit.
years.xp:
Ira Kaplan on the track list: "We made a decision at the last second just to leave the loud songs off."

Wikipedia reports generally favorable reviews; some critics also cited a lack of invention.

years.cap: Yo La Tengo at Landmark on Main Street, Port Washington, New York
years.h: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat Your Ass opens and closes on jams
years.p: Yo La Tengo's eleventh album puts two guitar jams of more than ten minutes at either end, with strings and horns between. It lands to universal acclaim.
years.xp: Informed by the band's soundtrack work, the album uses more strings and horns than earlier ones. Kaplan: "I think we gained an element of comfort with using that kind of instrumentation."
play: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat Your Ass
Pass the Hatchet, I Think I'm Goodkind

years.h: WFMU pledge callers get to pick the covers
years.p: For years the band took any request on the spot at WFMU's New Jersey radio pledge drive. Yo La Tengo Is Murdering the Classics collects the wreckage.

years.cap: Yo La Tengo at Tipitina's, New Orleans, 2007
years.h: The Freewheelin' Yo La Tengo takes requests and questions from the crowd
years.p: An acoustic tour where the audience asks for songs, and asks the band questions between them.
years.xp: Kaplan said the band tried answering questions "in a strategic manner so that the answers to the questions will lead to the next song."

years.cap: Yo La Tengo at Barby, Tel Aviv
years.h: The Condo Fucks debut at the Magnetic Field in Brooklyn
years.p: The trio plays under the alias in March. A year later Matador releases the garage-covers album Fuckbook.

years.h: Popular Songs debuts at No. 58 on the Billboard 200
years.p: The highest chart entry of the band's career to that point. Recorded in its New Jersey rehearsal space, with string arrangements by jazz composer Richard Evans on two songs.

eras.title: Still the same three
eras.text: Maxwell's closed and the Hanukkah shows moved on. The band kept releasing records on Matador, from a pandemic album recorded around one microphone to a return to noise in 2023.

years.h: Jesse Jarnow borrows a Painful song title for the band's biography
years.p: Big Day Coming traces Yo La Tengo and the rise of indie rock around it.

years.cap: Yo La Tengo at Sala Apolo, Barcelona
years.h: John McEntire of Tortoise produces Fade
years.p: [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] ends Roger Moutenot's run, which began with Painful in 1993.

years.h: Maxwell's closes, the Hoboken home of the Hanukkah shows
years.p: The club shuts in 2013. The Hanukkah shows later continue in Manhattan.

years.h: Yo La Tengo plays Bobby Night Ranger on Parks and Recreation
years.p: In the season 6 finale the band is an Indiana Night Ranger cover band. It also tours The Love Song of R. Buckminster Fuller with filmmaker Sam Green narrating live.

years.h: Dave Schramm returns for Stuff Like That There, a Fakebook sequel
years.p: Schramm rejoins for re-recorded old songs and covers of [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]], [[Hank Williams|906bddec-bc73-49f8-ac1e-eaee691c6cf9]] and [[Sun Ra|c27cac8e-4c4a-48c0-a4ba-41399b9c176d]].

years.cap: Robyn Hitchcock with Yo La Tengo
years.h: There's a Riot Going On borrows its title from Sly Stone
years.p: Pitchfork said the fifteenth album reflects the group's greatest and most instantly recognizable strengths.

years.h: The trio spreads out around one microphone for We Have Amnesia Sometimes
years.p: Over ten days in late April and early May 2020, they record five ambient instrumentals, socially distanced under New Jersey's pandemic rules.

years.h: Album seventeen, This Stupid World, nearly four decades in
years.p: On Matador, nearly forty years after the first single.
